cells.tense: You are here with your hands on it, and you are the one holding it up.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you keep meaning to fix and fix it today, then leave it alone. The doing doesn't need an audience.
cells.core:
You are the one holding this up, and it's plain enough from the outside. Not bracing, not straining — weight comes down on you and you stay upright. What you carry doesn't wobble, which is why people lean on it. The strength is in your body and the doing, and it reads as reliable because it is. Nothing here needs defending.

There's a next thing this can feed, and it isn't more weight. Someone near you is feeling their way through something, and you can set the load down long enough to be with them — not to carry it for them, just to be in the room. What keeps you upright doesn't stop being yours. It just gets shared for an hour.
cells.sheetLine: You hold it steady, and you get to name that.

cells.tense: You are already carrying what has not been handed to you yet.
cells.ask: Name one load you're holding that nobody asked you to hold. Set it down for a day and notice what actually happens.
cells.core:
You're holding things that haven't arrived. Before anyone asks, before it's yours to take, you've already shaped yourself to what could be needed — and all that effort goes to loads that may not come. Somewhere ahead there's a version of this where everything is finally secure, and you live there, so nothing now counts as finished.

That pressure is the load, not the job. The strength is real and it's running ahead of what's in front of you, which is why rest reads like neglect. Holding without forcing is still available. It looks like carrying what is actually here — one real thing, today — and letting the future keep its own weight until it shows up.

cells.tense: You stopped standing under it, and you're still at that door.
cells.ask: Finish one small thing completely — literally done, put away — and when it's done, let it go without starting the next.
cells.core:
There's something you used to stand under, and you set it down. Bearing it stopped being possible, so you stopped — and the strength didn't leave, it just went quiet. You can still stand. You're just not standing near anything heavy now, and the not-carrying has become the habit.

The way forward isn't to pick up more. It's to finish one thing and let the finishing be enough. Release that comes from completion, not from giving up. The strength returns through the door of something done, something set down, something that no longer needs you. One finished thing is enough to start.

cells.tense: The bearing is already happening, and you're calling it something else.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to one person, that you are the one holding this together. Then notice if the sentence feels true.
cells.core:
You're the one standing under this, and you've been doing it all along. People lean on it, the thing stays up, the load moves — and you talk about it like it's just how things are. Nobody assigned it. Nobody built the structure but you. The strength is running quietly and the credit is going to circumstance.

The strength is yours, and saying so isn't boasting. It's naming what is already true. Bearing it doesn't need to get heavier or lighter; it needs to be claimed. You built this and you're still under it. That's not a small thing, and it's not a fact about the world. It's a fact about you.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person already holds form under pressure; the record only says this capacity is seated in the Body house at Seed stage, which is a placement, not evidence of their history or what they have endured. A reader could reasonably say the read is wrong about what is happening now — that they are simply tired or busy, not braced against a future or standing behind a door — so the ask is written to be doable even if the diagnosis is off, and it asks for a small material act rather than a feeling. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is any line that tells them what their endurance has cost, since that is a story I cannot see from here.
